title: Why Does My PDF Look Blurry After Compression? 4 Ways to Fix It
metaDescription: Discover why PDF text and official seals turn fuzzy or pixelated after file compression. Learn how to preserve crisp text and sharp stamps while hitting strict 200KB or 300KB limits.
author: Zcompressor Engineering
heroHeadline: Why does my PDF look blurry after compression? (And how to fix it).
heroDescription: When reducing PDF file size for government portals, aggressive compressors often smudge official seals, signatures, and Roll Numbers. Here is how to keep text razor-sharp.

sections.heading: 1. Vector fonts vs downsampled raster images.
body: A PDF file contains two distinct types of visual elements: vector objects (fonts, lines, geometric curves) and raster bitmap images (photos, scanned sheets). True vector fonts never blur when compressed because they scale mathematically.

However, if you scan a paper marksheet using a smartphone camera, the entire page becomes a single flat raster image. When a compressor forces that image under a 200 KB or 300 KB threshold, it downsamples pixels and increases JPEG compression artifacts, causing fine text lines to blur.

sections.heading: 2. Never drop below 150 DPI for text certificates.
body: The standard for screen viewing is 72 DPI, but 72 DPI is disastrous for official certificates containing miniature registrar seals, Hindi/English bilingual text, or QR codes.

For government applications (UPSC, JoSAA, SSC, State PSCs), always preserve a minimum resolution of 150 DPI. At 150 DPI, text remains crisp and easily readable under 100% zoom while still fitting comfortably under strict size caps.

sections.heading: 3. Use intelligent quantization instead of blind pixel reduction.
body: Crude compressors shrink PDFs simply by halving image dimensions (e.g., cutting a 2000px height certificate to 800px). This destroys tabular marks columns and Roll Number digits.

Zcompressor uses adaptive DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform) quantization. It reduces background color noise and whitespace bits first while maintaining high-frequency edge contrast on dark typography and rubber stamps.

sections.heading: 4. Verify legibility at 100% zoom before portal submission.
body: Always preview your compressed PDF at 100% scale in your PDF viewer before hitting submit on any portal. Check whether your father's name, roll number, and issuing authority seal are clearly identifiable.
If the document is illegible, re-scan in grayscale or monochrome rather than trying to compress a blurry full-color scan.

faq.q: Can government portals reject an application if a certificate PDF is blurry?
faq.a: Yes. Scrutiny officers and automated document checkers routinely reject applications if candidate name, birth date, or official seals cannot be verified.

faq.q: What should I do if my marksheet is already blurry before compression?
faq.a: Wipe your smartphone camera lens, ensure bright indirect daylight, lay the document flat without glare, and re-scan using 150–200 DPI grayscale mode.
